requirements.evidence: Code cannot work: wrong trait namespace `use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\HasFactory;` (app/Models/Queue.php:8, app/Models/Ticket.php:10) is a fatal error on class load; duplicate `use App\Models\Entity;` (database/factories/QueueFactory.php:6 and :8) is a compile error. `#[Castable([...])]` (Queue.php:14, Ticket.php:18) is not an Eloquent cast mechanism and `casts()` returns `[]`, so is_active/labels_i18n/enum/datetime casts are absent and `$this->status !== TicketStatus::Waiting` (Ticket.php:71) is true for any ticket loaded from the DB, so call() always throws. `$user->entity_memberships()` (Ticket.php:76) is not a shown relation. TicketFactory computes the code for a separate new queue (`Ticket::nextCode(Queue::factory()->create()->id)`, TicketFactory.php:28) and forQueue() does not reallocate it, so two forQueue tickets both get A001 and violate the unique index. nextCode orders by numeric cast, not insertion order (Ticket.php:53). The collision retry is DB::transaction(..., 5) (IssueTicket.php:44), which does not retry unique violations.

conventions.evidence: Authorization in Ticket::call is an inline membership query plus a manual `throw new AuthorizationException()` (Ticket.php:74-79) instead of a policy/gate. Migration timestamps `2026_10_29_000000`/`000001` with no trailing newline suggest hand-written migrations. docs/business-rules.md:432-433 adds only a generic persistence sentence and none of the queue/ticket rules (code sequence, write-once, single call); there is no CHANGELOG entry. On the positive side, the action lives in app/Actions, models use #[Fillable] like Entity, and both migrations have down().

security.evidence: Mass assignment is deliberate (#[Fillable] on both models). The membership check in call() fails closed but does not go through a policy. call() reads and writes status without a row lock (Ticket.php:71-83), so two concurrent calls can both pass the Waiting check and break the single-call invariant. No user input surfaces or output escaping are involved.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files: no Pest tests for nextCode edge cases, inactive-queue rejection, negative priority, write-once, single call, or unauthorized call, even though the conventions require that everything implemented ships with a test.

simplicity.evidence: The save() override for write-once (Ticket.php:89-100) and the action are reasonably direct. Downsides: empty `casts()` methods alongside a fake attribute (Queue.php:19-22, Ticket.php:30-33); `$ticket = null` with a by-reference closure instead of returning from DB::transaction (IssueTicket.php:28-45); manual padding branch (Ticket.php:60-63), where str_pad alone already handles numbers ≥1000; a redundant 'called_by_user_id' => 'integer' cast.

readability.evidence: Unused, nonexistent imports `Illuminate\Support\Facades\DateTime` and `Illuminate\Contracts\Validation\ValidationException` (Ticket.php:14-15); redundant same-namespace imports `use App\Models\Queue;` (Entity.php:106) and `use App\Models\Ticket;` (Queue.php:10); FQCN exceptions inline; misleading empty casts(). The names and method sizes themselves are fine.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task (migrations, models, enums, exception, action, factories, docs); there are no unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\HasFactory` does not exist (the trait is `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory`), so both models fail fatally on load.
`use App\Models\Entity;` is imported twice, which is a PHP compile error.
Casts are declared through a nonexistent `#[Castable]` attribute while `casts()` returns [], so no casts are applied; status stays a string after load and call() always throws LogicException.
No tests ship with the change, which violates the project's mandatory TDD convention.
The factory computes the code for a separately created throwaway queue and forQueue() does not reallocate it, so two forQueue tickets both get A001 and hit the unique index.
`$user->entity_memberships()` is not a shown User relation, so call() will likely throw BadMethodCallException.
nextCode picks the highest numeric suffix via a MySQL-style CAST instead of the last valid code by insertion order, and `like 'A%'` lets malformed codes such as 'A12B' be parsed as valid.
DB::transaction attempts only retry on deadlocks, not on a unique (queue_id, code) collision, so the required collision retry is not implemented.
call() checks and sets status without locking, so concurrent calls can both succeed.
Authorization is a hand-rolled membership query instead of a policy/gate.
The business-rules doc does not describe the implemented queue/ticket rules, and there is no CHANGELOG entry.
The migrations look hand-written (synthetic timestamps, no trailing newline) rather than generated with make:migration.
Redundant import of a class in the same namespace.

review.summary: The change adds migrations, Queue/Ticket models, enums, the IssueTicket action, factories and brief doc notes for queue ticket issuance. It cannot run: the HasFactory namespace is wrong, QueueFactory has a duplicate import, and the casts are not applied, so call() always fails. The ticket factory produces duplicate codes and no tests are included at all, so the PR should be rejected.
